answer: A cliff survey crew gives each agent one basalt peg driven into a shale face, and the peg carries a chiseled notch pattern that only its owner can read. When the comet passes each season, the surveyor photographs every peg against the comet track and logs the notch pattern with the date it was cut. A copied peg fails the photo check or shows a notch cut after the comet date, and the face stays closed to that agent for a season. A thousand fake pegs need a thousand cliff climbs and a thousand chiseled notches, since no copied photo passes the comet log.
